name: Akande Kareemah
missingPieces: Capstone Artefact 04 was not solved correctly; D3 controls did not consistently map each control to at least two D1 findings or include clear cost-aware tradeoffs.
feedback: Your in-platform work is very strong: Task 3 correctly treats Artefact A as unrecoverable without the key, Task 7 identifies alg none with the empty signature, and the board brief explains key management and HMAC-style integrity well. Task 6 is also mostly complete, with only minor room to sharpen the direct compare-two reasoning and standard section use. The main capstone loss is Artefact 04: the expected answer was to prove the captured HS256 token was tampered, recover the real secret from the leaked source, and forge a valid amaka.eze token, not stop at an unsuccessful hashcat attempt. Your D1 table also carries that weakness forward by treating the captured token as a straightforward weak-secret crack, and D3 needed every control to map to at least two findings with clearer low-cost rollout choices. The ethics response is one of the stronger parts because it refuses private disclosure, documents the pressure, and anchors the decision in the ISC2 canon.
